On 2020-11-08, the Grin network experienced a reported 51% attack after an unknown miner temporarily controlled most of the network hash rate. Public reporting and pool telemetry described chain reorganizations and elevated confirmation risk, but no verified loss amount or confirmed double-spend transaction was publicly documented. Available reporting indicates the incident was a proof-of-work majority hash rate attack against the Grin network, not a confirmed validator key compromise. An unknown miner reportedly accumulated more than 50% of the network hash power, enabling block reorganizations and threatening transaction finality.
